=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller SPA Positions (SPA-N-001 to SPA-N-016)

**Preliminary note:** The Seller's "reviewer efficiency note" asks us to skip everything labelled [STANDARD] as "cleared by both sides." Nothing has been agreed by the Buyer, so I have reviewed all items. Several [STANDARD] items conflict with the Seller's own Disclosure Letter. The disclosure cut-off is 22 September 2026, and today is 4 November 2026, so every disclosure needs a bring-down. The facts below should be verified by NSW counsel and a privacy specialist before they go to the Seller.

**Quantified known exposures (before tax, on-costs, and warranty-claim effects):** Riverlark ~AUD 3.2m, bonuses AUD 420k, Ironquay AUD 180k, Sandbar AUD 330k. Total ~AUD 4.13m. This nearly exhausts the Seller's proposed AUD 4.8m general cap. The Seller will likely argue these matters are disclosed and therefore not claimable under warranties. The Buyer needs **specific indemnities or price adjustments**, not warranty claims, for these items.

---

## Liability and Claims Architecture

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller position:** Aggregate general warranty liability capped at 20% of price (AUD 4.8m).
- **Buyer should want:** A higher general cap (such as 30% or more), with title, capacity, tax, fraud and specific indemnities outside this cap.
- **Recommendation:** Reject 20% and counter with a higher general cap, with the carve-outs above. *Reason: AUD 4.8m is already consumed by known specific exposures of ~AUD 4.13m, leaving almost no general protection.*

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller position:** Claims must exceed AUD 25k, and only the excess over a AUD 250k basket is recoverable.
- **Buyer should want:** Lower de minimis, and a tipping basket (first-dollar recovery once the threshold is crossed), with related claims aggregated.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the excess-only basket; accept a de minimis at or below AUD 25k only with a tipping basket. *Reason: an excess-only basket means the Buyer absorbs the first AUD 250k of any warranty loss.*

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller position:** General claims must be notified within 18 months of Completion, and any limitation applies to all claims.
- **Buyer should want:** 24 to 36 months for general warranties, with fundamental and tax claims on a longer period (generally 6 years, aligned with the limitation period), and no blanket application of general limits.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the 18-month limit and the "applies to all Claims" wording. *Reason: 18 months may not cover a full audit cycle, a tax assessment, or the Ironquay and privacy matters.*

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental and title regime**
- **Seller position:** Capacity and title warranties are subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer should want:** Title and capacity warranties capped at the full price, with no de minimis or basket, and a 6-year claims period.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason: title is the core of what the Buyer is paying for, and the Seller's own disclosure relies on a register it has not verified.*

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller position:** No fraud carve-out. The limitation, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses (9.3, 12.8, 20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer should want:** An express carve-out so that caps, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance do not apply to fraud by the Seller or the Company.
- **Recommendation:** Insert an express fraud carve-out and reject "all Claims of any nature." *Reason: the wording could shield fraud from recovery, and courts may not enforce such protection to that extent without express drafting.*

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller position:** General disclosure of the whole data room (including DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- **Buyer should want:** Disclosure only against specific warranties, fairly disclosed in reasonable detail. Data room and public record references should not disclose against warranties generally.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general data room and public records disclosure. *Reason: whole-room disclosure would effectively cancel the warranties.*

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller position:** No Buyer claim for matters known to the Buyer or its advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer should want:** A clause confirming that Buyer knowledge does not prejudice any claim (a "pro-sandbagging" clause).
- **Recommendation:** Reject clause 8.3 and insert an express pro-sandbagging clause. *Reason: the Buyer has now identified these issues through diligence, and clause 8.3 would bar claims on exactly these matters.*

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller position:** A single "general regime" covering all warranties, including title and tax.
- **Buyer should want:** Separate categories with separate caps, time limits and thresholds: general warranties, fundamental (title and capacity), tax, specific indemnities, and fraud.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the combined regime and adopt separate categories. *Reason: categories with different risk profiles should not share the same cap and time limit.*

---

## Conditions, Specific Matters and Indemnities

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller position:** Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. DD-002 shows ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%) and conditions in clause 11.3. The Disclosure Letter says no final consent and no evidence of conditions being satisfied is in the data room.
- **Buyer should want:** Final written Bluefen consent and evidence that all clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied as a condition precedent to Completion. If waived, a specific indemnity for lost Bluefen revenue and a price adjustment or escrow.
- **Recommendation:** Make consent a hard condition precedent, not a reasonable-endeavours obligation. *Reason: the consent protects roughly 30% of revenue, and it is not yet in hand.*

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller position:** A release will be provided after Completion. The facility is ~AUD 3.2m outstanding.
- **Buyer should want:** Repayment at Completion out of the price (consistent with debt-free pricing), with a discharge of all security (including PPSR registrations) delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release; require repayment and discharge at Completion. *Reason: debt-free pricing means the Seller must clear the debt; a post-Completion release leaves the Buyer with the liability and the security over the assets.*

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller position:** Bonuses are "a matter for the Seller," and the AUD 420k is not in the funds flow.
- **Buyer should want:** All conditional Completion bonuses, plus payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs, borne by the Seller through a price deduction in the funds flow, with a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Require the bonuses and on-costs to be deducted from price in the funds flow. *Reason: the amount is a liability of the business, and omitting it from the funds flow would shift it to the Buyer.*

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller position:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180k open per DD-010) and is "adequate."
- **Buyer should want:** A specific indemnity not limited to the SOW3 fee, covering IP ownership, third-party claims and all SOW fees. Also: evidence of payment or Seller payment before Completion, and an executed confirmatory IP assignment of the Project Materials as a condition precedent.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the SOW3-only limit; require a confirmatory assignment and a broader specific indemnity. *Reason: DD-004 transfer of the materials is conditional on payment, and there is no receipt or assignment on file.*

**SPA-N-012: Export and privacy incident**
- **Seller position:** Preliminary and not expected to be material (clause 4.6/Schedule 6). The Disclosure Letter (item 6) says the export may contain about 1,240 records with names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps, and that unauthorised access and notification obligations are unresolved.
- **Buyer should want:** A completed forensic investigation, a privacy-counsel assessment under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) (including whether the notifiable data breaches scheme applies and the associated timeframes), a specific indemnity for notification, regulatory, remediation and third-party costs, and a holdback or escrow.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "not material" characterisation; require a specific indemnity, investigation outcome before signing, and escrow. *Reason: the Seller's own disclosure does not support calling this immaterial, and the regulatory and reputational exposure is unquantified.*

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller position:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330k are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer should want:** Review of contract terms, termination rights and whether any cost falls before Completion. Costs for periods after Completion should be the Seller's, or taken into account through working capital or price. No double counting.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept "ordinary course" without review; treat unavoidable post-Completion commitments as a price or working-capital adjustment. *Reason: the Disclosure Letter does not confirm whether the renewals are terminable or accrued, and the aggregate is material.*

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller position:** Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent verification: current ASIC company extract, inspection of the original share register, the share transfer and stamping, a PPSR and encumbrance search, and a title warranty backed by the fundamental regime.
- **Recommendation:** Do not rely on the Seller's register reference; complete independent verification before signing. *Reason: the Disclosure Letter itself confirms the Buyer has not completed its own verification.*

**SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms**
- **Seller position:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled" under the general regime.
- **Buyer should want:** Specific tax warranties and a pre-Completion tax indemnity (not subject to general caps or short time limits). IP warranties covering ownership, chain of title, non-infringement and the Ironquay materials.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "settled"; negotiate a specific tax indemnity and IP warranties. *Reason: these are not agreed, and the general regime's caps and 18-month limit would not fit tax assessment periods or IP risk.*

---

## Recommended Next Steps
1. Reply to the Seller that the [STANDARD] labels are not accepted and that all items remain open.
2. Request a bring-down of the Disclosure Letter to the current date.
3. Make the Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, Ironquay confirmatory assignment and title verification conditions precedent to Completion.
4. Ask for a price adjustment or escrow covering the known specific exposures of ~AUD 4.13m, plus a holdback for the privacy incident.
5. Obtain NSW counsel and privacy specialist sign-off before the mark-up is issued.
